description.summary: blur what is behind parts of a surface

protocol.description:
This protocol lets clients ask the compositor to draw a blurred copy of whatever is below parts of their surfaces (frosted glass), for translucent panels, menus and title bars.
Note: this is a downstream extension maintained with the Pangolin desktop, it is not part of upstream river.

entry.name: blur_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a river_blur_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Existing river_blur_v1 objects are not affected.

request.name: get_blur
request.description: Create the blur object of a surface. A surface has at most one.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The blur goes away with the next commit of the surface.

request.name: set_regions
request.description:
Set the parts of the surface behind which the compositor blurs, as a list of rounded rectangles in surface-local coordinates. Each entry is nine 32 bit integers: x, y, width, height, the radii of the top left, top right, bottom right and bottom left corners and the opacity of the blur from 0 to 10000. An empty array removes the blur.
Double-buffered state, applied on the next wl_surface.commit.

request.name: reveal

description.summary: animate a part of the surface into view

request.description:
Animate the given part of the surface (e.g. a popup) from the given state to where it is, at the refresh rate of the outputs. Until the animation ends the compositor hides that part in place and draws it transformed instead, following what the surface commits; blurred regions inside the part move along.
The start state is the part scaled by scale/10000 around its center, moved by dx, dy, with opacity opacity/10000. The animation follows the CSS timing function cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2), each value divided by 10000.
Takes effect immediately, not on commit, so that the content drawn by the next commit is already animated. Starting an animation ends those it overlaps.

request.name: conceal

description.summary: animate a part of the surface out of view

request.description:
Animate the given part of the surface, as currently shown, to the given end state (same arguments as reveal), at the refresh rate of the outputs. The compositor keeps a copy of the part and its blurred regions as they are now and draws it above the surface, which goes on showing what it commits (typically without the part).
Takes effect immediately, not on commit. Starting an animation ends those it overlaps.

request.name: set_cutouts

description.summary: round the corners of the window above

request.description:
For a surface drawn right below a window (a decoration below it, such as a shadow): makes the window look rounded by drawing, above the window, what is behind it (this surface included) where the window's corners are cut off.
A list of rounded rectangles in surface-local coordinates, the window's shape. Each entry is six 32 bit integers: x, y, width, height, the radius of the corners, and which corners are rounded (bits: 1 top left, 2 top right, 4 bottom right, 8 bottom left). An empty array removes the cutouts.
Double-buffered state, applied on the next wl_surface.commit.
